conviction_note: The bar is well sourced and the Q3 lines the company guided (consulting mid-to-high single digits, about $95m fiduciary income, immaterial FX, more margin expansion in Q4 than Q3) sit inside consensus. The only new information since Marsh last spoke is mixed and second-hand. Gallagher's Sept-25 color on US retail property renewals improving from -12% to -7% is a mild positive for Marsh Risk. The mid-year reinsurance rate-on-line falling 16% is a mild negative for a small Guy Carpenter quarter. Findings sum to +0.3. The scaled number is (2x0.52-1)x4.0 = +0.16 because nothing decides the sign: p_up 52 leans slightly up on the peer read, against a +2.9-vol-point put skew and a -8.5% reaction to last year's similar Q3.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.96, revenue $6.63B, consolidated underlying growth 3.9% (Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-10-12: https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/curious-marsh-mrsh-q3-performance-121505139.html ; Zacks preview 2026-10-09: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/marsh-beat-q3-earnings-risk-150900027.html). Other sources agree within a cent: Earnings Whispers EPS $1.96 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/MRSH) and Benzinga $1.97 / $6.65B (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MRSH/earnings-forecasts). Segment bars (Zacks): R&IS underlying 3.5% (Q2 actual 3%), Marsh Management Consulting 7.1%, total Consulting 4.7%, Guy Carpenter revenue $400m (+0.5%), fiduciary interest income $95.1m. The company guided FY26 underlying growth 'similar to 2025' (1H26 4%), consulting Q3 mid-to-high single digits and fiduciary income about $95m. Two agreeing sources and a company guide, so sizes are not capped for the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.55-1.6% of float, 2.4 days to cover (Benzinga/Equibles, around 2026-08-20; https://equibles.com/stocks/mrsh/shortinterest , https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MRSH). Another Benzinga reading on 08-28 gave 4.3 DTC on a different volume base. Not crowded. Skew_25d +2.92 vol points ('downside paid', moderate). Put/call OI 1.12. Event-implied move 3.36%, but the ATM spread is 44% of mid, so it is indicative only. Run-up +2.6% over 5d and +0.8% over 20d. The stock is 13.9% below its 52-week high, and down from $192.64 on 2026-08-28 (Benzinga) to $178.20. Sell-side consensus is Hold. Citi downgraded to Neutral on 2026-07-21.

findings.finding: Gallagher spoke on 2026-09-25, after Marsh's 2026-07-21 call. US retail property renewal premiums fell about 7% in Jul-Aug against -12% in Q2, casualty rose 5%, and US retail ex-property rose about 4%. Gallagher expects Q3 brokerage organic growth of about 5%. That points to Marsh Risk (Q2 underlying 4%, US/Canada 4%) holding at least its Q2 pace. The Zacks bar for R&IS underlying is 3.5%, against 3% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: R&IS underlying growth is the line this stock trades on. In Q3 2025 the segment slowed to 3% from 4% and its margin was flat; the stock fell 8.52% (baseline, Reuters: https://de.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com%2C2025%3Anewsml_L3N3VX0OT%3A0-marsh-mclennan-s-flat-operating-margins-in-risk-and-insurance-unit-drags-on-shares). In Q2 2026 R&IS grew 3% with Guy Carpenter at -2%, and the stock went -0.28% on the day (Barchart: -3.1% next session).
findings.why_not_priced: This is peer color from a September Q&A, not a Marsh number, and Gallagher's management said the property improvement was 'mainly renewal timing and business mix, not a fundamental shift'. The R&IS consensus already moved up to 3.5% from the Q2 actual of 3%, so part of it is in the bar. If the market had fully priced an R&IS reacceleration, the skew would not be paying for downside and the stock would not be off 7% since late August.
findings.independence: Marsh's own Q2 2026 Global Insurance Market Index (rates -6%, property -12%, US +1%) is a broader series and points the other way on pricing: https://www.marsh.com/en/corp/about/news/global-commercial-insurance-falls-6-percent-q2-2026.html . None confirms the improvement independently.

findings.finding: Guy Carpenter's own report puts the global property-cat rate-on-line index down about 16% at the mid-year 2026 renewals, an acceleration from -12% at 1 January. Guy Carpenter revenue fell 2% underlying in Q2 and was flat in 1H. Consensus still has Q3 Guy Carpenter revenue up 0.5% (about $400m of $6.63B).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Barchart attributed the Q2 2026 next-session dip of 3.1% to 'weakness at Guy Carpenter, continued reinsurance pricing pressure' (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3381048/marsh-nysemrsh-exceeds-q2-cy2026-expectations).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The index is public, and management told investors not to extrapolate Q2 because the second half is 'much smaller' with a different mix. A +0.5% consensus on a business whose rate headwind accelerated is the part that may be stale. Guy Carpenter is about 6% of Q3 revenue, so the rest of the company only has to grow at bar for this to wash. This finding is sized net of that.
findings.independence: Reinsurance News on the same index: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/global-property-cat-rates-down-16-as-softening-extends-into-july-renewals-guy-carpenter/ (same underlying document). JP Morgan said there was no near-term floor: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/reinsurance/news/breaking-news/jp-morgan-sees-no-nearterm-floor-as-reinsurance-rates-fall-16-at-midyear-581535.aspx

findings.finding: Mercer Wealth fees track asset levels. The S&P 500 rose about 15% in Q2 2026 and about 2% in Q3, and Mercer Wealth grew 8% underlying in Q2 with AUM at $846bn at June 30. Zacks consensus has total Mercer revenue growth of only 3.7%, against 5% underlying in both Q2 and 1H.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction attributed to Mercer. Consulting has not been the line the stock trades on in the cited coverage.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed. Fee lags and mix (Health 3%, Career 2% in Q2) can absorb it. If the market had priced it, the Mercer consensus would sit near the 5% run rate rather than 3.7%.
findings.independence: Marsh's Q2 release gives Wealth +8% and the Q2 call gives AUM of $846bn: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000062709/000006270926000193/mmc2q2026ex991newsrelease.htm . Mercer's mix is a different document from the market data.

findings.finding: Accenture's quarter to 2026-08-31, reported 2026-10-01, is a read on consulting demand after Marsh last spoke. Consulting revenue was $9.28bn, up 6% in USD, and consulting bookings were $9.4bn with total book-to-bill of 1.2. That is broadly steady discretionary demand for Oliver Wyman.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: total consulting grew 5% underlying while the stock fell 8.5% on R&IS, so consulting has not carried the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Accenture is an IT-services proxy for a strategy consultancy, with a different client mix. Marsh flagged a Middle East slowdown that Accenture does not capture. The consulting consensus (7.1%) already sits inside Marsh's mid-to-high single digit guide.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call Marsh guided Q3 Marsh Management Consulting underlying growth to mid-to-high single digits, citing a 'healthy backlog' but slower Middle East sales in Q2. It guided fiduciary interest income to about $95m and said FX is immaterial. Consensus is 7.1% and $95.13m, inside both guides.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction to a consulting or fiduciary surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The consensus matches the guide line for line, and the finding is filed so the panel can see the bar is guided. The residual risk is the Middle East caveat: Q3 2026 saw a 'more uncertain geopolitical outlook', with energy the best sector at +17%.

findings.finding: Marsh guided 'more margin expansion in the fourth quarter than in the third quarter'. A flat R&IS margin in Q3 2025 (24.7%, missing estimates) drove that print's -8.5% reaction. Zacks consensus has R&IS adjusted operating income up 5.6% on revenue up 4.1%, which implies about 40bp of margin expansion in a quarter the company has steered toward less.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: a flat R&IS margin and a slowdown gave -8.52% (baseline and Reuters).
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is public, but the consensus R&IS operating income still embeds expansion, so a flat margin would be a miss on the line that sank the stock last October. The put skew is consistent with some of this being priced.

findings.finding: Marsh has beaten consensus EPS in each of the last four quarters, by an average of 4.1%. Zacks ESP is +0.42%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The beats drew mixed reactions: Q2 2026 -0.28%, Q1 2026 +4.39%, Q4 2025 +5.47%, Q3 2025 -8.52% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the wire copy and largely priced. EPS beats are routine for this name, and its reaction turns on underlying growth and margin.

findings.finding: Peer Brown & Brown guided H2 2026 Retail organic growth to 1.5-2.5% and Specialty Distribution to 2-4% on 2026-07-28, after Marsh's call, with cat-property rates falling 15-35%. That is evidence of softening middle-market broker growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction of MRSH to peer guides.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is two and a half months old, and BRO's mix (small commercial, wholesale property) is far more property-exposed than Marsh's large-account book. Gallagher's later color is fresher and points the other way.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest is low (about 1.6% of float, 2.4 days to cover), sell-side consensus is Hold after Citi's July downgrade, and the stock fell from $192.64 (2026-08-28) to $178.20 into the print. That is a modestly de-risked setup against a moderate +2.9-vol-point put skew.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q1 2026, with the stock near lows, it rose +4.39% on a 4% organic print.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown since late August has no identified cause, so this is sized small. The skew still pays for downside, which says the market is not positioned for a relief rally.
findings.independence: Equibles short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/mrsh/shortinterest . MarketBeat Hold consensus: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MRSH/forecast/

baseline_tension: The mild net-positive peer read (Gallagher property renewals improving) cuts slightly against a moderate +2.9-vol-point put skew and last October's -8.5% on a similar Q3. With no guide change expected and a small run-up, p_up sits at 52, near the non-result.
lessons_applied: Rule 9, segment net of the rest: the Guy Carpenter negative went from -0.4 to -0.3 because Guy Carpenter is about 6% of Q3 revenue.
Rule 3, own caveat reaches the number: Gallagher's peer finding went from +0.4 to +0.3 because Gallagher itself called the property improvement timing and mix.
Rule 5, macro-to-company proxy: Mercer's equity-market finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 5, unexplained drawdown worth little: the positioning finding went from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rule 6, inside the guide: the fiduciary-income and consulting-guide items were merged into one finding at 0 (draft had two zero-sized items), since they come from one call document.
